decisions.boundary_condition: Do not apply to rooms requested with separate beds for occupants or to multi-room requests where a particular room has a separate-bed setup.
decisions.canonical_value: queen-size or better main hotel bed
decisions.condition: When selecting a hotel room bed type and a single main bed is appropriate.
decisions.default_action: Request a queen-size or larger main bed; accept a king-size bed as satisfying or upgrading this preference.
decisions.exception_condition: If the current request specifies an explicit layout, such as a queen bed plus a pull-out couch or two twins, preserve that layout instead of converting it to a queen-or-better single-bed room.
decisions.name: Queen-or-better hotel bed default
decisions.rationale: Repeated examples state a queen-size-or-better or queen/king main-bed requirement. This is a distinct bed-size threshold, not an alias for a king-first preference, and its layout and separate-bed exceptions prevent overgeneralizing.

decisions.boundary_condition: Applies only to hotel room bed type. Do not infer room count, destination, dates, view, balcony, price, party size, or other amenities from this preference.
decisions.canonical_value: king-size hotel bed preferred, with queen or other suitable beds acceptable when needed
decisions.condition: When searching for a hotel room or specifying room amenities and no separate-bed arrangement is required.
decisions.default_action: Look first for, or request, a room with a king-size bed when it fits the current hotel constraints.
decisions.exception_condition: If the current request asks for a different bed arrangement, if occupants need separate beds, or if no king-bed option satisfies the required constraints, follow the current request or present suitable non-king alternatives such as a queen bed instead of blocking the booking.
decisions.name: Prefer king-size hotel bed when available
decisions.preference_value: king-size bed preferred; queen-size or another suitable bed acceptable as a fallback
decisions.rationale: Both candidates encode the same hotel bed-size default: prefer or request a king-size bed when bed type is selectable. The merged policy keeps it as a soft default because the evidence includes queen-or-king formulations and availability/current-request exceptions.

decisions.boundary_condition: This applies only to bed count; it does not establish a fixed mattress size, location preference, smoking preference, or other hotel amenity requirement.
decisions.canonical_value: one-bed hotel room when multiple beds are not needed
decisions.condition: When searching for a hotel room and the stated party or sleeping needs do not require multiple beds.
decisions.default_action: Request a room with exactly one bed, leaving the mattress size flexible unless separately specified.
decisions.exception_condition: Override the one-bed default if the party needs separate beds, if the user explicitly asks for multiple beds, or if no one-bed room satisfies the hard hotel constraints.
decisions.name: Prefer one-bed hotel rooms
decisions.preference_value: exactly one bed in the hotel room
decisions.rationale: The supporting examples consistently specify a single king or single queen bed. This is a bed-count preference independent of mattress size, so it should remain separate from the bed-size policies.
